findings.title: Metric alert handler is abstract and crashes when constructed
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and has an empty body. StatefulDetectorHandler still has abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data), so instantiating MetricAlertDetectorHandler raises TypeError. The class remains MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler constructs it for any detector whose slug is metric_alert_fire. Previously this was a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned an empty list. process_detectors does not catch that TypeError, so one such detector aborts the whole batch instead of no-opping. Implement the abstract methods, or keep a concrete DetectorHandler until a real stateful implementation exists.

findings.title: Fired occurrence fingerprint is not tied to the resolve fingerprint
findings.body: On a non-OK transition, evaluate_group_key_value publishes whatever IssueOccurrence build_occurrence_and_event_data returns, and it never sets or checks occurrence.fingerprint. On the later OK transition it publishes a StatusChangeMessage whose fingerprint is always build_fingerprint(group_key) (`{detector_id}` or `{detector_id}:{group_key}`). Issue resolution matches on that fingerprint. The new hook is not given the fingerprint, and the abstract method does not require the subclass to use build_fingerprint, so an occurrence opened under any other fingerprint will not be resolved when the detector returns to OK. Pass build_fingerprint(group_key) into the hook or overwrite the returned occurrence's fingerprint before publishing.

findings.title: Occurrences are published before dedupe and detector state are committed
findings.body: process_detectors sends each result to Kafka via create_issue_occurrence_from_result and only then calls handler.commit_state_updates(), which is what persists the dedupe value and active/priority transition queued during evaluate. This PR is what starts attaching an IssueOccurrence to threshold breaches on that path. If publish raises on a later group key, or the process stops before the commit, the dedupe key and stored status are unchanged. The same packet is evaluated again as a new transition and another occurrence is emitted. Occurrence ids are chosen by the subclass and are not derived from detector id, group key, and dedupe value, so the retry is not idempotent and users can get duplicate issues.

findings.title: Group-key unit test expects an occurrence for a different key
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. The handler forwards that group key into build_occurrence_and_event_data, which puts it on the occurrence fingerprint (`{detector_id}:group_key` versus the expected `{detector_id}:val1`). DetectorEvaluationResult and IssueOccurrence compare by value, so this assertion fails. Build the expected occurrence with group_key "group_key" and value 10.

findings.title: Occurrence tests never assert the measured value
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value and never uses it, and MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data only forwards to that helper. Assertions therefore stay green if evaluate passes the wrong measurement. Concrete mismatches already in the tests: test_state_results_multi_group has group_2=10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6; test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6; TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6. Put value on the occurrence (for example evidence_data) and pass the actual packet value, or the new hook argument is untested.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate's docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. This PR changes the return type to a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Callers that follow the docstring will iterate keys or treat the result as a sequence of evaluation objects. Update the docstring to describe the dict.
